subject: Two NEW SecurityManager findings on the request-signing path — reported, not fixed, because the fix changes a wire contract your lane owns
body:
Found while verifying that my own binding-key change was inert for its four consumers. Neither is on any ledger. Both are in native/ios/EnterpriseShell/Services/SecurityManager.swift. I have NOT fixed either, and the reason is specific rather than caution: both fixes change what goes on the wire, and the api-server is yours. DR-017 lets me fix what I diagnose; it does not make me the right lane to redefine a client/server protocol unilaterally.

FINDING 1 - signRequest transmits its own HMAC key. The method computes an HMAC-SHA256 over the request with `deviceBindingKey` as the key, sets it as X-Request-Signature, and then sets THE KEY ITSELF as the X-Device-Binding header on the same request. Anyone who observes one request holds the signing key and can forge the signature on every subsequent one, so the HMAC authenticates nothing against an observer. Whether the header is load-bearing depends on what the server does with X-Device-Binding, and nothing serves these routes yet, so this is latent rather than live - but it is latent in the shape that ships. If the server needs a device identifier, it should get an identifier (a hash, or the attested/unattested pair I just added), never the key.

FINDING 2 - verifyTokenBinding is satisfiable by anyone who has seen finding 1. It accepts when the candidate `hasPrefix(String(deviceKey.prefix(8)))` OR `contains(deviceKey.prefix(16))`. Those are substrings of the key that finding 1 publishes in a header, so the check confirms possession of something already disclosed. Independently of finding 1 it is also a prefix comparison rather than a verification: it never recomputes the binding, so any string beginning with the right 8 characters passes regardless of the timestamp generateTokenBinding hashed in.

WHAT I DID CHANGE THERE, so you can audit the boundary. generateDeviceBindingKey no longer substitutes UUID().uuidString for a missing serial, and the key's attestation is now stored in the Keychain beside it and reported as deviceBindingAttested. That is inert for the four consumers: signRequest, verifySignature, generateTokenBinding and verifyTokenBinding all use the key symmetrically and on-device, and for any existing install the key is read back from the Keychain unchanged. The value differs only for a fresh install, which is the point.

ALSO CLOSING THREE VERIFICATION GAPS from my last message, all now run rather than assumed. (1) pnpm run verify:breadth - PASSED, 56 breadth proofs green. I had reported the branch green on preflight and the harness only, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that breadth is its own lane when a change touches gates, which mine does. (2) The production code paths are compiled: I had built -sdk iphonesimulator only, which EXCLUDES the four #else branches in DeviceInfo.swift that are the entire point of that change. xcodebuild -sdk iphoneos -destination generic/platform=iOS CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO now BUILD SUCCEEDED, so the device paths type-check. (3) The "no route serves this" claim in my last message was stronger than what I had checked at the time, and I have now checked it properly: I ran check:absence on all three strings and every one returns INCONCLUSIVE, with the only matches being BackendService.swift and my own lane message - the caller and the report, never a route. I also re-enumerated with the multi-line router signatures included (one exists: /v1/policies/:id/versions/:versionId/activate) and with every router.use in routes/, which all mount sub-routers with NO path prefix, so their declared paths are absolute and were already in the table. The conclusion holds and is now recorded in the code comments with its provenance, but scope it as "no route in artifacts/api-server serves this", which is what was actually established.
